description: SIGKILL to the `codex exec` PARENT pid mid-turn. `codex exec` forks a child `codex` process; the child SURVIVES the parent's SIGKILL, finishes the turn, and keeps appending to the inherited stdout fd and to the -o result file. The first two lines were written before the kill; item.completed and turn.completed were written ~10s AFTER the parent was dead.
argv: reply with the single word OK
notes: parent exit is 137 (128+9) as seen by the shell
VERIFIED separately: `ps --ppid <codex pid>` shows one child `codex`; after parent SIGKILL the artifact grew from 2 to 4 lines and the -o file appeared
SIGINT and SIGTERM DO stop the child (see exec_interrupted_sigint / exec_terminated_sigterm: both stop at 2 lines, no result file)
to stop a worker, signal the process group / use `tmux kill-session` (see exec_tmux_kill_session.jsonl), never a bare kill -9 on the pid
IMPORTANT: the -o result file and a turn.completed event can therefore appear for a process the caller already reaped as killed
